html:
Kamarupa was the first historical kingdom of Assam, in the Brahmaputra valley, from about 350 to about 1140. It appears on the maps from 600 to 1200.

Its name first appears in Samudragupta's inscription on the Allahabad pillar, as a frontier kingdom that paid him tribute. Three dynasties ruled it in turn: the Varmans, the Mlechchhas and the Palas of Kamarupa. Their capitals lay along the Brahmaputra, near today's Guwahati and Tezpur. The goddess temple of Kamakhya stood here.

Its best known king, Bhaskaravarman, allied with Harsha against Shashanka of Gauda and hosted the Chinese monk Xuanzang around 640. In the 12th century the kingdom broke up into smaller states. In the 13th century the Ahoms arrived in the east of the valley and later built the Ahom kingdom.
sum: Kamarupa was the first historical kingdom of Assam, in the Brahmaputra valley, from about 350 to about 1140. It appears on the maps from 600 to 1200.
